issue_context.title: networkd reverts to link-local addresses after a few days
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**

 > systemd 251 (251.1-1-arch)

<!-- **NOTE:** Do not submit bug reports about anything but the two most recently released *major* systemd versions upstream! -->

**Used distribution**
 > Arch Linux

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
<!-- Make sure to enclose the pasted kernel version in `backticks`, so that
     GitHub doesn't convert the `#` character typically included in it into a
     reference to old GitHub issues. -->
 > 5.17.9-arch1-1

**CPU architecture issue was seen on**
 > amd64

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > networkd to keep my connection up

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > After a few days networkd only renewed fe80:: 

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 > Connect to a network and leave it running for a few days

**Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue**

I've pasted details of my VPS and debug logs up to the failure: https://gist.github.com/Jookia/ece8bb0ef6d71718ff3d0632781f4421
I can provide the full log but it's 464M, I would have to compress it.

The fail seems to be:

```
Jun 03 04:22:05 blane.jookia.org systemd-networkd[920]: ens3: ndisc_check_ready(): SLAAC addresses and routes are not set.
Jun 03 04:22:05 blane.jookia.org systemd-networkd[920]: ens3: ndisc_check_ready(): SLAAC addresses and routes are not set.

Jun 03 04:22:05 blane.jookia.org systemd-networkd[920]: ens3: State changed: configured -> failed
Jun 03 04:22:05 blane.jookia.org systemd-networkd[920]: Sent message type=signal sender=n/a destination=n/a path=/org/freedesktop/network1/link/_32 interface=org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties member=PropertiesChanged cookie=21 reply_cookie=0 signature=sa{sv}as error-name=n/a error-message=n/a
```

Then it stops renewing IPv6 and IPv4 addresses.

Possibly the same issue as #23467

Edit: Unit file:

```
[Match]
Type=ether

[Network]
IPv6PrivacyExtensions=Yes
IPv6AcceptRA=yes
DHCP=yes
DNS=2001:4860:4860::8888 8.8.8.8
```
comments:
I experience a similar issue for a longer while now - first I thought I misconfigured the dhcpv6 server, but now it is correct and works for a long time - until some reboot of a router and systemd-networkd seems to run into a failed state.
Internal LAN router with OpenWRT - reboot happened on Jun 04 at about 04:00 AM - I use graylog to debug this and other stuff... but since this "headless" device runs graylog and looses the connection, my log is incomplete.

I tried to compensate the lost connection with `ActivationPolicy=always-up` - but it obviously doesn't help.

I assume that the dhcpv6 server did not get a renew from the outer DHCP (WAN -> external modem/router -> internal LAN) - so it probably sent some failed message to systemd-networkd and networkd completely failed the interface.

`systemd 251 (251-1-arch)`
`Arch Linux`
`5.15.37-1-lts`
`amd64`

This just means you have a compiler version mismatch (as the error message says). Either building with gcc11 or rebuilding gnu-efi with the compiler you're using to build sd-boot should do the trick (arch already did a rebuild for gnu-efi for this reason).
